target_customer: Hardware engineers and startups that need small-batch printed circuit board assembly quickly
problem: Conventional contract manufacturers are slow and awkward for small orders; the About page says the idea came from founders' frustration with them.
business_model: Per-order manufacturing and assembly with instant quotes, plus parts sourcing
product_category: On-demand electronics manufacturing and robotic PCB assembly

founders.name: Andrew Seddon
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page, he led computer vision and robotics teams at his prior employers.

technical_complexity.rationale: Quote software was moderate, but building and running an automated assembly line with levitating movers needs robotics, process control and supply chain work.

defensibility.rationale: The Grid factory and parts stock are capital intensive to copy, though early on the service was ordinary outsourced assembly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied it according to the sources read; the company remained independent and announced a Series A in May 2026.

market_need_then: Hardware startups and makers were multiplying around 2012 and the founders cite their own frustration with contract manufacturers as the origin; no dated demand statistics were found.

branding.domain_note: Main site is circuithub.com; later variant domains redirect to it per BuiltWith.

identity.logo: Wordmark with strict usage rules in a published brand guide
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and engineer-to-engineer, with quarterly first-time-right figures published.

branding.community_and_virality: Appears on podcasts such as The Amp Hour and lists customers like Tesla and Formlabs on its site.

brand_strength.rationale: Known among hardware engineers with a clear brand guide and customer logos, but no evidence of broader awareness.

pivots.from: Online marketplace and quoting for outsourced PCB assembly
pivots.to: Own automated factory called The Grid
pivots.why: Per the company site, it now runs its own robotic factory in Massachusetts; the date and original model were not sourced

outcome_analysis: CircuitHub spent over a decade raising modestly, about 20 million dollars quietly from angels by its own account, while building an automated factory. It announced a 28 million dollar Series A in May 2026 led by Plural, which took total raised to about 48 million. It is active with no exit.
notes: Company page names no co-founders; search summaries mention Rehno Lindeque and Jon Friedman but no opened source confirmed it, so they are not listed. Earlier funding: the company's post says about 20M was raised quietly from super angels, and its About page cites 18M with Y Combinator and Google Ventures; no individual earlier round with date was found. Founding year ranges 2011 to 2013 across sources. No dated 2012 competitor sources were found. The pivot entry is inferred from the current site and is undated.
